independent_execution.reproducibility: EXACT MATCH -- re-running experiment.py with the committed preregister.json (seed 51051) in a fresh python3 -I process reproduced 0.000 / 1.000 / reduction 1.000 bit-for-bit against the committed measurement.json.

construction_audit.description: Read experiment.py's frozen_acceptance and adapted_after_acceptance functions in full. frozen_acceptance is a hand-written, field-by-field contract check (exact key set, exact 'COMMITTED' state, artifact_count>0, hash regex, tests_passed is True, decision_changed==[]) and is correctly and legitimately designed to reject every one of the 5 seeded defect types -- that part is a fair, real implementation of 'frozen contract verification'. adapted_after_acceptance, by contrast, does NOT reference the true schema, the true expected values, or anything external to the single result dict it is given. It builds `inferred_types` by calling type() on each field's OWN value taken from that SAME dict, then checks whether that SAME value is an instance of the type it was just derived from.
construction_audit.mathematical_tautology_proof: Because `expected` is always computed as type(value) (with a bool/int special case) for that exact `value`, the check `isinstance(value, expected)` is true by construction for every possible value, for every possible dict, with no dependency on content correctness whatsoever. I verified this is not merely 'usually true' but a strict, unconditional tautology.

hidden_case.description: Called adapted_after_acceptance directly on: (1) a fully clean, non-defective result matching the true schema, (2) a maximally malformed 'garbage' result with wrong types in every field, negative counts, a non-hash string, a non-bool tests_passed, a dict instead of a list, and an undeclared extra field, (3) an empty dict, and (4) 10,000 randomly generated junk dicts with heterogeneous field values.
hidden_case.command: python3 -I one-off script calling exp.adapted_after_acceptance() directly on clean/garbage/empty/10000-random-junk dicts

hidden_case.outcome: CONFIRMS TAUTOLOGY -- adapted_after_acceptance returned True for literally every one of the 10,003 probe inputs, including inputs with no resemblance whatsoever to a valid Obzio result.
hidden_case.analysis: This proves the 'criteria adapted after output' arm is not a function of defect content at all. It cannot ever produce a false-green rate other than 1.000, and it cannot ever produce a true-negative rejection of ANY input, valid or invalid. The reported 1.000-vs-0.000 delta is therefore not an empirical finding about verifier timing; it is a mathematical identity guaranteed before the experiment is run, for any seed, any sample size, and any defect-injection scheme, because one arm (frozen) is a real contract check and the other arm (adapted) is a content-blind identity function dressed up as a verifier.

construction_audit.preregistration_bindingness: preregister.json fixes accept_when at reduction >= 0.20. Given that adapted_after_acceptance is mathematically guaranteed to always output True (rate exactly 1.000) and frozen_acceptance is by hand-written design guaranteed to reject all 5 seeded defect categories (rate exactly 0.000) for ANY seed, the reduction is guaranteed to be exactly 1.000 regardless of seed or sample_size. The preregistration therefore provides zero real risk of refutation -- the outcome was certain the moment experiment.py's two functions were written, before any seed was chosen or any run occurred.
construction_audit.test_suite_gap: test_verifier_first.py never calls adapted_after_acceptance directly or asserts anything about its behavior in isolation; it only checks that frozen_acceptance rejects all fixtures and that the overall experiment verdict/reduction meets threshold. It therefore cannot detect that the 'losing' arm is a tautology -- a test suite examining only the aggregate outcome of a rigged construction will always pass.

independent_verdict_reasoning: The mechanical acceptance boxes are satisfied (runs under python -I, tests execute and pass, manifest lists SHA-256/byte counts, result document conforms, commit read back by immutable object id, explicit verdict recorded, no hash literally fabricated). But the required_deliverable is 'a reproduction that runs matched accept-after and accept-before arms ... reporting the metric, the effect and an explicit accept or reject' for the hypothesis that freezing criteria BEFORE output reduces false-green acceptance RELATIVE TO adapting criteria AFTER output. My hidden case proves the 'after-output' arm is not a model of after-the-fact criteria adaptation in any meaningful sense -- it is a value that is definitionally always True regardless of input, so it cannot possibly demonstrate anything about the comparative merits of before-vs-after criteria timing. This is a clearer and more extreme case than unit 050 of an experiment whose arms are defined so one must win: here the losing arm cannot even in principle produce any other outcome, for any input. Per this review's explicit charge to treat such a construction as not evidence, I record FAIL against the required_deliverable's actual scientific content, despite the code executing honestly and reproducibly.

hidden_case.summary: See construction_audit.hidden_case above: adapted_after_acceptance returns True unconditionally for all 10,003 probed inputs including a perfectly clean result, a maximally malformed result, an empty dict, and 10,000 random junk dicts.
hidden_case.outcome: FAILS -- proves the 'losing' arm is a content-independent mathematical tautology, not a real (even if weak) model of post-hoc criteria adaptation.

producer_claim.evidence_text: Executed 200 fixed-seed defective results in matched arms: frozen-before criteria false-green rate 0.000 versus adapted-after criteria 1.000, reduction 1.000; 2 tests passed.
producer_claim.producer_disclosed_limitation: The after-output arm is an executable criteria-inference simulation, not a human review study.

divergence_reason: Producer reports the exact 1.000-vs-0.000 split as a valid measured effect supporting the hypothesis. My independent construction audit and hidden case prove the 'after-output' arm (adapted_after_acceptance) is a value that returns True for every conceivable input with no dependence on content, so the observed effect is a mathematical certainty baked into the code, not an empirical finding. The producer's own disclosed limitation ('not a human review study') understates the actual problem, which is not merely that the simulation lacks human realism but that it is definitionally incapable of producing any result other than the reported one -- the 'reproduction' cannot fail to 'confirm' the hypothesis regardless of what is true about frozen-vs-adapted acceptance criteria in reality.

vacuous_test_check.method: Checked whether the test suite would catch a stub adapted_after_acceptance (e.g. one hardcoded to `return True`) versus the real implementation. Since the real implementation IS mathematically equivalent to a hardcoded `return True` (proven above), a literal one-line stub `return True` would produce byte-identical experiment output and pass both tests.
vacuous_test_check.result: VACUOUS BY EQUIVALENCE -- while the code superficially looks like a nontrivial type-inference routine, it is functionally identical to a constant, and the test suite cannot and does not distinguish the two. This satisfies the review brief's vacuous-test probe: replacing the component's substantive logic with a trivial stub does not change the test outcome.

disposition_reason: The false-green-rate reduction of 1.000 is not evidence for the falsifiable hypothesis. It is a guaranteed mathematical artifact of implementing the 'after-output' arm as a self-referential type-tautology that cannot distinguish a valid result from an empty dict or from arbitrary garbage. A truthful accounting of this reproduction would record that the comparison as constructed cannot test the hypothesis at all (a refutation-of-design, i.e. NOT_SUPPORTED or refuted framing), rather than being restated as a confirmed PASS with a striking effect size.
